title: Bombay HC: Patent Office Cannot Reject a Claim on Unsourced 'Common Knowledge'
case_name: Deepak Nitrite Limited v. Assistant Controller General of Patents and Designs
citation: Commercial Miscellaneous Petition No. 107 of 2025, decided 6 July 2026
card_summary: The Patent Office refused Deepak Nitrite's sodium nitrite application by invoking common general knowledge without naming its source. Justice Arif Doctor set aside the refusal and remanded the matter, holding a Controller cannot reject a claim on common general knowledge unless the order names the source and shows it predates the priority date. The court criticised orders that merely reproduce an examiner's report.
card_tip: A patent refusal that invokes common general knowledge without naming and dating a source is open to challenge on that ground alone; an unsourced assertion will not survive scrutiny.
verification_notes: Parties, docket number, the food-grade sodium nitrite application, the 6 July 2026 decision date, and the holding on sourcing and dating common general knowledge are consistent across LiveLawBiz, BananaIP and King Stubb & Kasiva. The ruling is a single-judge decision applying earlier Delhi High Court authority on the point, not a new appellate rule.
